original_value: AbstractProbabilistic risk assessment techniques are the important tools which can considerably improve the safety performance of the studied system and reduce the risk to an acceptable level. Typically, decision‐making process is an important part of risk assessment methods that accordingly bring the ambiguity inside. Decision makers as experts commonly express their subjective opinions about the occurrence of the root events in order to obtain the probability of the undesired event. Subsequently, the critical root events are identified, and possible intervention is performed to reduce the probability of the critical events. However, the serious point is the viability of the obtained probabilities and priority ranking of the critical events. In this study, a heuristic optimization model of linear mathematical programming using triangular intuitionistic fuzzy number (TrIFN) is proposed to obtain the feasible, optimum, and reliable results compared with available methods. The Spearman correlation is performed to examine the reliability and behavior of the proposed model. In order to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach, it is applied on a real case study. The application of the model confirms its robustness to prioritize critical root events over the conventional one.

result.paraphrase: Abstract probabilistic risk assessment techniques are essential tools for substantially improving the safety performance of the system under study and reducing risk to an acceptable level. In general, decision making is a key component of risk assessment methods, and it introduces ambiguity into the process. Experts and decision makers usually provide subjective judgments on the occurrence of root events to estimate the probability of the undesired event. The critical root events are then identified, and appropriate interventions are carried out to lower the likelihood of these events. However, the main concern is whether the calculated probabilities and the resulting priority ranking of critical events are valid. In this study, a heuristic optimization model based on linear mathematical programming and triangular intuitionistic fuzzy numbers (TrIFN) is proposed to obtain feasible, optimal, and reliable results compared with existing methods. Spearman correlation is used to evaluate the reliability and behavior of the proposed model. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, it is applied to a real case study. The results confirm that the model is robust in prioritizing critical root events compared with the conventional approach.
